findings.title: Propagate non-disappearance directory scanning failures
findings.evidence: logical_bytes calls os.walk without onerror. Python walk silently ignores directory scan errors by default, so a denied/unreadable subtree can produce an incomplete size accepted by polling/tail/post-write budget checks. lstat ENOENT handling only protects individual removed files, not a failed directory enumeration.
findings.requestedFix: Use the already reviewed small directory-error callback policy: tolerate only transient ENOENT disappearance; propagate every other scan error so supervision fails and safe cleanup still runs. Keep symlink nontraversal and actual file accounting.

findings.title: Route parent soft termination through owned-group cleanup
findings.evidence: Popen launches a new session, while the Python parent has no SIGTERM handler. Default SIGTERM can terminate the parent without executing run finally, leaving the independent worker/Vitest group alive. Catching BaseException only handles Python exceptions; it does not replace default signal termination.
findings.requestedFix: Reuse the previously reviewed minimal soft-stop recorder approach for SIGTERM/SIGINT: install before owned runtime, stop work, mark failure even if signal arrives during cleanup, preserve the normal reap/absence/scratch/report path and restore prior handlers in outer finally. Do not throw repeated asynchronous exceptions inside cleanup or alter group ownership.
